newsitem.title: FINLAND: Valmet CEO sees growth in service ops.
newsitem.headline: Valmet CEO sees growth in service ops.

text.p: Services and paper machine rebuilding will grow faster than the market for new machines, Matti Sundberg, CEO of Finnish paper machine maker Valmet Oy said on Wednesday.

"I can see a future in which just one fifth of our net sales would come from new machines, without giving up any of our market share (in new machines)," Sundberg told a news conference on Valmet's 1996 results.
"We should achieve annual growth of ten percent on the service side without any acquisitions," Sundberg said.
Valmet's 1996 profit after financial items rose 66 percent on 1995 to 1.1 billion markka while sales grew 37 percent to 11.8 billion markka.
Income from service operations alone -- excluding major rebuilds -- rose 17 percent to 1.4 billion markka from 1.2 billion in 1995, Valmet said.
"Last year we had 30 big rebuilding projects, while we delivered only about ten new machines," Sundberg said. "We believe this trend will continue in the future."
Valmet booked 13 orders for complete paper and board machines in 1996 and delivered 11 machines, Valmet said.
"Rebuilding and servicing operations are less sensitive to buisiness cycles," Sundberg said.
Valmet has plenty of scope to increase its servicing and rebuiding business without having to start servicing machines built by competitors, he said.
"We have 800 machines running worldwide... (but) we only service about 15 percent of them," he said. @
To develop service in Southeast Asia, Valmet is building a board and paper machine technology centre in Thailand which will be opened in late summer, Valmet said.

Valmet is one of world's three largest paper machine makers -- Harnishfeger unit Beloit Corporation and Voith Sulzer Papiertechnik are the two others -- and not interested in acquiring any smaller players in the business, Sundberg said.
"I think they would be more of a headache than a benefit," he said.
Valmet does, however, see opportunities for acquisitive expansion in its automation and power transmission businesses, Sundberg said, but did not elaborate.
The automation business provided 12 percent of group net sales in 1996, and power transmission two percent, it said.

Looking at the prospects for the paper industry where Valmet's clients are, Sundberg said paper consumption can be expected grow in all markets, but above all in Asia where consumption could even double by 2010.
Asked about the outlook for paper prices, Sundberg said they were heading upwards, but that it was difficult to say whether that would happen early or late in the year.
